{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABdOQcxQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhGvmoE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 243, "title": "Add multi-graph library with named graphs, editor selection, and execution-target assignments", "body": "## Goal

Allow users to **save, manage and select multiple independent processing graphs**, based on the **third approved UI concept: “Graph Library”**.

This is the foundation for having different saved graphs for **Live transcription** and the **future in-page Web voice typing** UX. Implement the management experience now, without implementing in-page microphone buttons or simultaneous multi-graph execution in this task.

## UX / layout (use the third mockup)

Keep the existing light visual language, page header/navigation and compact controls. Introduce a **Graph Library** management screen, with the following primary hierarchy:

```text
Graph Library
[Search graphs…] [Sort] [Filter]                [Import] [+ New graph]
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Name              Purpose      Updated      Required models  State │
│ Voice Typing      ...          ...          ...              ...   │
│ Meeting Notes     ...          ...          ...              ...   │
│ Live Translate    ...          ...          ...              ...   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌────────────────────────────┐  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
│ Default execution targets  │  │ Selected graph: Meeting Notes     │
│                            │  │ Description + preview of nodes    │
│ Live         [graph ▼]     │  │ [Edit/open] [Duplicate] [Delete] │
│ Web voice    [graph ▼]     │  │                                   │
└────────────────────────────┘  └───────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Upper area:** a compact, searchable list/table of named graphs, showing **name, purpose/short description, last updated, required model names, and a grounded readiness status**. Select a row to update details. On narrow windows, use responsive compact rows rather than horizontal overflow that hides primary actions.
- **Bottom-left:** simple **Default execution targets** with dropdowns for **Live** and **Web page voice typing**. Store assignments by stable graph ID, not by display name. Clearly mark the Web voice input feature **not yet available** until its separate implementation; showing a future assignment must not claim on-page voice typing is functional.
- **Bottom-right:** selected graph title, description, small noninteractive graph schematic/preview, and **Edit/Open**, **Duplicate**, **Delete** actions. Reuse the real graph's nodes and edges for preview; do not invent node types or model names. If preview rendering is expensive, use a deliberately lightweight read-only visualization.
- **Top actions:** **New graph**, **Import graph JSON**, search, simple sorting (name/recent) and limited filtering where useful. Avoid unnecessary UI clutter.
- **Navigation:** make Graph Library easy to reach from the existing Live / Graph / Models navigation. **Graph Editor remains the current full-canvas editor**, opened for the selected library graph; allow return to Library and identify the current graph by name.
- **Intentionally omit** workspaces, detailed version history, tagging systems, elaborate favorite systems and extra graph status dashboards in this first iteration; these were mockup ideas, **not** required functionality.

## Graph library behavior

- Support **New**, **Rename**, **Edit**, **Duplicate**, **Delete**, **Import as new**, and **Export** for individual named graphs.
- Maintain stable, unique **graph IDs**, independent of editable graph names and of the existing *node IDs* (which remain scoped to each graph).
- Preserve each graph's existing **version 15 graph schema, node IDs, positions, settings, named ports, edges and validation semantics**. Library metadata (graph ID, name, description, timestamps and assignments) belongs *outside* graph JSON, preserving import/export compatibility.
- Open a selected graph in the existing editor; Save updates **only that graph** (not the currently assigned Live graph unless it is the same ID). Discard/Load saved/Reset/import-in-editor apply to the **selected graph draft**, never any other library entry. Surface unsaved-change warnings before switching away.
- Duplicate a graph's validated data to a **new ID** with a sensible editable name. Import a standard existing graph JSON as a **new library entry**; reject malformed/unsupported data with clear errors, leaving all existing graphs untouched. Export retains the familiar portable graph JSON.
- Destructive delete requires confirmation, cannot silently remove an execution-target assignment, and must leave a viable fallback. Either block deletion of an assigned graph until reassignment or guide explicit reassignment first. Never delete the last usable graph accidentally.
- One graph's invalid data must not silently replace other valid entries, break library browsing, or overwrite the corrupt original. Offer recovery/export of the original where appropriate.

## Existing installations / storage migration (critical)

Current implementation persists **one graph** at `localStorage['processing-graph-v1']` via `extension/graph.js` (`readGraph`/`saveGraph`). `extension/graph-page.js` and `extension/recorder.js` read that same key; other tabs may edit it concurrently.

- On upgrade, **losslessly migrate the existing saved graph into one named library entry**, preserving its content and making it the initially assigned **Live** graph. Do **not** replace it with a default example, change its graph version, or lose the user's work.
- Make migration idempotent and safe under concurrent page opens, reload, interrupted writes, storage limits and malformed legacy JSON. **Do not discard or silently overwrite** the legacy key or invalid source while recovery is unresolved. Have deterministic fallback if migration cannot be committed.
- For brand-new installations, create one clearly named default Live transcription graph from `defaultGraph()`; **do not assume Web voice typing is already runnable**. Users can create a Voice Typing graph when appropriate.
- Store the library and target assignments in a coherent, validated, versioned representation; use atomic-ish updates and existing `navigator.locks` / stale-revision/conflict detection to avoid lost edits across Graph Editor, Library, Live and multiple tabs.
- Surface storage conflicts clearly and preserve dirty drafts; do not resolve them by silently overwriting another graph.
- Existing tests and call sites using `readGraph`/`saveGraph` should be updated or given explicit compatibility behavior. Never silently read a different selected graph than the one the user expects.

## Execution target selection / Live

- Assign **one graph as the Live default** from Graph Library, saved persistently by graph ID.
- Opening Live resolves that **exact selected saved graph** and prepares **only the executable model instances for it** under the current Live preload lifecycle (#239). Graph Save still downloads/verifies required model files, including parked model nodes in the graph being saved; no GPU/model inference is started in Graph Library.
- When the Live assignment changes while idle or preparing, cancel/dispose stale model preparation safely and prepare the newly selected graph before enabling Start. The UI must unambiguously show which named graph Live is using.
- When a session is running, preserve its immutable active graph and **never hot-swap** it because of library edits, deletion requests or changed default assignment. Apply the new assigned graph **only to the next session** after normal Stop/Cancel. Maintain microphone/speaker permission gestures, graph actions, display and other existing session behavior.
- Assign a **Web voice typing default graph ID** for future use, but **do not implement in-page mic UI, in-page session startup, target selection, or concurrent execution** as part of this Issue. The saved assignment must be separately addressable by the eventual implementation.
- Multiple graphs are **saved/managed**, but **simultaneous independent graph execution is out of scope** for this phase. Do not add a new global GPU/Worker pool or reuse one active session across two graph IDs.

## Model status / readiness semantics

- Table's **required models** are derived from actual graph model requirements; do not hardcode examples from the mockup.
- Distinguish file cache **Ready/Needs preparation/Error/Unknown** from **Live runtime/GPU ready**. Do not show an unconditional “Ready” badge just because a graph is saved, or start model loading when browsing the library.
- Saving a selected graph should prepare model assets according to the existing Graph Save lifecycle. Models page remains the place for global asset recovery and cache inspection. A model shared by two saved graphs must be cached once by asset identity, not downloaded separately for each graph.

## Implementation guidance

Likely touch points:
- `extension/graph.js` single-key persistence and graph validation; create a small dedicated library/assignment storage module rather than overloading the executable graph schema.
- `extension/graph-page.js` / `extension/graph-editor.js` selected graph context, per-graph drafts and save.
- `extension/graph-editor.html`, new Library page/script and navigation styles.
- `extension/recorder.js` + `extension/session.js` default Live graph resolution, graph-name display, safe session/preload switching.
- `extension/graph-model-preparation.js` / model status as required, while preserving existing file-cache semantics.
- Extension/browser unit/E2E tests, docs and navigation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Graph Library follows the **third approved mockup**: compact search/filter/list at top, **default execution assignments lower-left**, selected graph preview/actions lower-right, consistent with existing styling.
- [ ] Can create, rename, duplicate, edit, delete (with safeguards), import and export independent named graphs; selection and persistence survive reload.
- [ ] Editing/saving graph A never changes graph B or its metadata; unsaved drafts and cross-tab conflicts are handled without data loss.
- [ ] Existing single `processing-graph-v1` installs migrate **losslessly and idempotently** to the library; invalid legacy data remains recoverable.
- [ ] Live default assignment persists; Live opens/starts the **correct selected graph** and prepares exactly its applicable models, respecting #239.
- [ ] Changing Live default during an active session does not switch that session; the next session uses the newly assigned graph.
- [ ] Web voice typing assignment is storable and labeled **not yet implemented**; no false claim that on-page dictation exists.
- [ ] Deleting an assigned or last graph cannot leave a dangling/invalid silent default; clear warnings and recovery exist.
- [ ] Graph JSON structure and node execution semantics are unchanged; file cache deduplication, Save preparation, graph actions, keyboard accessibility, responsive layout and MV3 navigation remain functional.
- [ ] Automated tests cover migration/corrupt legacy, CRUD, duplicate IDs, import/export, edit isolation, assignments, storage conflicts, Live selection/active-session immutability, preload cancellation, and browser UI; record the tests actually run.

## Out of scope

- In-page microphone button / Content Script voice typing UX (future task).
- Multiple Live sessions or simultaneous execution of multiple graphs.
- Version history, workspaces, graph marketplace, new AI models, new Node types, graph execution engine redesign.
